A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCM-GRPO work, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The original Appendix A is retained as Appendix D in v3; the additional material can be distinguished reliably from relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracies, an optimization-strategy ablation, and empirical analyses of generated reasoning structures in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds reward ablations, sensitivity and training-stability results, and a structural-faithfulness evaluation.

M1.justification: Both versions retain teacher-distilled structured chains, parent-before-child graph construction, SFT, and GRPO with the same correctness, structure, and length rewards in Equations (1)-(8). The SCM-inspired reframing and newly specified implementation details do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions cover HoVer 2-4-hop and EX-FEVER 2-3-hop verification in Table 1 and retain Figure 1's 1-3-hop analysis. Additional model scores and reward experiments do not introduce another dataset, domain, or task scenario.

E2.justification: v3 adds ProgramFC to the Qwen3-8B comparison in Table 1; v1 reports ProgramFC only in the GPT-3.5 block. The other named comparators remain. Decoding-time length penalties and reranking are discussed without reported comparative evaluations.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends evaluation design through reward-removal controls and sweeps over correctness rewards, reward weights, and token-length intervals in Tables 2 and 4. Appendix C adds a whole-chain DAG and parent-validity metric, and Table 1 adds the matched-backbone ProgramFC evaluation. Newly disclosed settings for retained experiments do not establish that those experiments changed.

E4.justification: v1 compares SFT, CPO, and GRPO and analyzes structural correlations. v3 retains these analyses while adding tests of individual reward contributions, hyperparameter sensitivity, training instability, and structural faithfulness. These directly investigate the proposed reward design and its failure conditions.

E5.justification: Table 3 newly reports a training-reward dispersion statistic, 'Reward last std.' of 0.259. This does not establish repeated-run uncertainty. The existing significance tests and correlations in Figure 6 remain unchanged, and neither version reports benchmark confidence intervals or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: v3 fills missing Qwen EX-FEVER scores and adds Qwen3-8B ProgramFC results averaging 64.31%. New reward experiments report 0.7544 accuracy with full rewards, 0.7427 without Rs, and 0.6433 without Rl; Appendix C reports structural faithfulness above 95%. SCM-GRPO's main-table average remains 71.02%, and the original optimization and structural-analysis results are retained.

T1.justification: The model tuple, DAG construction constraint, and mathematical objectives in Equations (1)-(8) are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or derivation is added. The causal-to-structural reframing changes interpretation, while the new faithfulness evaluation applies existing graph-validity constraints.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions change the central claim from a formal causal-inference framework to SCM-inspired dependency-graph reasoning, explicitly excluding interventions and counterfactual semantics. Claims of robust generalization and logical consistency give way to structural traceability, although benchmark-superiority claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 removes v1's assertion that topological ordering guarantees hallucination-free reasoning and limits the benefit to structural transparency and fewer unsupported steps. It adds interpretations of reward instability and inference-cost tradeoffs, and corrects the appendix's claim that a linear relationship implies exponential complexity growth. Dependence on teacher data and unverified generalization beyond four hops remain acknowledged.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the teacher, the 60% training-query seed subset, 10,539 generated candidates, and rejection counts. Appendix A supplies a prompt and output template; Section 3.5 explains tokenized length and training-data-based interval estimation. Tables 3-4 disclose 1,700 RL steps and concrete reward and length settings that v1 leaves unspecified.

R1.justification: v3 adds Graph of Thoughts and Verify-and-Edit, replaces citations to different works with HoVer, EX-FEVER, Search-o1, and Qwen3 source papers, and removes several infrastructure and other references. It also substantially narrows the novelty positioning from causal inference to explicit structural dependencies. Metadata updates to retained works are separate from these substantive changes.

P1.justification: v3 edits terminology and passages across the abstract, introduction, methods, results, and conclusion while retaining the main section order and much of the original prose. It organizes the expanded appendix into A-D and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. Author, affiliation, correspondence, and running-header text also change.

P2.justification: The compact optimization-only Table 2 becomes a full-width, grouped ablation table with a training-status column, supplemented by new stability and sensitivity Tables 3-4. Figure 1 is redrawn with clearer labels and a substantially expanded caption. Figures 2-7 retain their underlying graphics but are repositioned and receive caption revisions.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially improves claim-evidence alignment by replacing unsupported causal and hallucination-free guarantees with a bounded structural interpretation. The matched-backbone comparison, reward-component tests, and concrete implementation disclosures address important weaknesses in v1's validation and reproducibility. Main accuracy scores do not improve, and the new faithfulness result still lacks a stated sample size and uncertainty, but these remaining gaps do not outweigh the substantial gains.
